root_cause: The tabbable library (src/index.js) contains an invalid CSS selector 'details>summary:first-of-type' in its candidateSelectors array and in the isHidden function. When the focus trap calls tabbable(container), it invokes querySelectorAll with a selector list that includes this invalid pseudo-class, causing a DOMException. This prevents the focus trap from computing tabbable nodes and moving initial focus into the dialog.
repair_strategy: Replace the invalid selector 'details>summary:first-of-type' with the valid CSS selector 'details>summary:first-child' in both occurrences within src/index.js. This allows querySelectorAll to succeed and the focus trap to find the first tabbable element (#street).
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can open the address dialog and have focus automatically move to the first focusable field (street address), satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Minimal risk: the change only corrects an invalid CSS selector. The tabbable library may have relied on the invalid selector for some edge case, but 'details>summary:first-child' is the standard selector for the summary element.
verification_requirements: Run the frozen journey to confirm focus moves to #street after opening the dialog.
Verify that the dialog still traps focus correctly (Tab cycles within dialog, Escape closes).
Ensure no regression in other focus trap behaviors.
